candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 16:1-8. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On the Deuteronomic recapitulation of Passover — 'Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover unto the Lord thy God' (Deu 16:1) — Ephrem reads the THIRD Mosaic Passover legislation (after Exo 12 and Num 9) as the canonical triple-witness that Pascha is the non-negotiable hinge of the covenant year. The repetition is not redundant but emphatic: the Lord wills that Israel never forget the month of deliverance. Tewahedo Fasika theology cites Exo 12 + Num 9:2 + Deu 16:1 as the canonical triple-Mosaic anchor that the yearly Pascha is constitutive of covenant identity — eucharistically fulfilled in the Tewahedo Holy-Week Anaphora.

On the Deuteronomic recapitulation of Passover — 'Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover unto the Lord thy God' (Deu 16:1) — Ephrem reads the THIRD Mosaic Passover legislation (after Exo 12 and Num 9) as the canonical triple-witness that Pascha is the non-negotiable hinge of the covenant year. The repetition is not redundant but emphatic: the Lord wills that Israel never forget the month of deliverance. Tewahedo Fasika theology cites Exo 12 + Num 9:2 + Deu 16:1 as the canonical triple-Mosaic anchor that the yearly Pascha is constitutive of covenant identity — eucharistically fulfilled in the Tewahedo Holy-Week Anaphora.
